Issued at 230 AM EST Sun Nov 22 2026

Today-Monday...Mid-level troughing lifts northeastward early this
morning towards the Carolinas, with quasi-zonal flow developing 
aloft across Florida. At the surface, the low currently near the 
Florida-Georgia border will lift northeastward, with its attendant
cold front weakening and drifting southward across the Florida 
peninsula today, ushering in a drier air mass locally with PWATs 
falling to around 1". This drier air mass will linger into Monday 
as a broad area of high pressure develops across the Gulf. 
Westerly flow develops areawide behind the weak boundary today, 
staying around 10 mph through the period with some locally higher 
gusts possible at times. By Monday, winds become more northerly 
around 5 to 10 mph. The drier air mass will result in rain 
chances remaining below 10% areawide today through Monday, giving
east central Florida a much needed break from the rainfall. The 
weak cold front will change temperatures very minimally, with 
highs ranging from the mid 70s up north to the low 80s down south 
today and in the 70s areawide on Monday. Overnight, temperatures 
remain in the 60s, with some locations across far northern Volusia
and Lake potentially dropping into the upper 50s.

While seas and swells will begin to gradually subside today as 
the low pulls farther away, a high risk of rip currents will 
continue along the entire east central Florida coast. Rough surf 
also remains a concern. Entering the ocean is not advised! By 
Monday, a moderate risk of rip currents is forecast at all local 
beaches.

Tuesday-Wednesday...A mid-level trough begins strengthening 
across the Midwest on Tuesday, with energy aloft spreading 
eastward towards Florida. By Wednesday, the trough becomes a cut-
off low, digging southeastward towards north Florida. At the 
surface, an area of low pressure located near Mississippi and 
Alabama will drift eastward across north Florida on Tuesday, with 
its attendant cold front slowly drifting across the Gulf. By 
Tuesday night, model guidance indicates the potential for a broad 
low to develop in the southeastern Gulf along the frontal 
boundary, lifting northeastward across the Florida peninsula into 
Wednesday. It is important to note that global models are handling
the development of this low in very different fashions, meaning 
there is a level of uncertainty with this next potential event. 
Overall, trends keep this disturbance moving across the area much 
faster than recent notable events.

Ahead of the front, winds shift to out of the northeast locally, 
helping to advect moisture from the Atlantic towards the Florida 
peninsula. PWATs are forecast to recover to around 1.4-1.6" 
areawide through Tuesday afternoon, surging to 1.7-2.0" as the low
develops and lifts across the state. Rain chances increase, 
peaking at 40-70% on Wednesday. At this time, it remains too early
to determine exact rainfall amounts across east central Florida 
due to the uncertainty between models. However, given the ongoing 
flooding along the east central Florida coast and saturated soils 
due to recent rainfall, additional flooding will be a concern. 
There is a low chance for storm development on Wednesday, with 
around a 20% chance of lightning strikes and strong wind gusts 
with the strongest activity. Exact hazards will become clearer 
over the next couple of days. Showers and storms will diminish 
across east central Florida into Wednesday night, moving offshore 
as the low lifts farther northeast and away from the area. 
Temperatures will remain near normal in the 70s each afternoon, 
falling into the 60s Tuesday night and the mid 50s to mid 60s 
Wednesday night.

A period of high astronomical tides is also anticipated to return
to the east central Florida coast mid week, with current trends 
favoring the potential for some minor coastal flooding starting on
Wednesday. Periods of high tide will see the greatest impacts, 
particularly during the morning high tide cycle. 

Thursday-Saturday...The mid-level low becomes more trough-like as
it digs southward across the Florida peninsula on Thursday, 
lifting the surface low farther northeastward and away from 
Florida through Thursday. Drier air settles behind the low across 
the peninsula, with local rain chances currently forecast to 
remain below 20% Thursday through Friday. By next weekend, global 
models indicate a low chance for some showers as a weak boundary 
meanders across the peninsula, but there remains uncertainty this 
far out. Temperatures are forecast to remain near to even slightly
below normal through the extended period. Lingering high 
astronomical tides through the end of the week may continue to 
produce minor coastal flooding during high tide.
